content.title: About
content.content: Potato French fries are thin strips or wedges of potato that are deep‑fried until golden and crispy. They are a staple side dish and snack in fast food, often served with a variety of dipping sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first documented recipe for fries appeared in Belgium in the late 19th century.
In the United States they are called "French fries" despite their Belgian origin.
There are many variations: classic, double‑fried, sweet potato, and herb‑seasoned versions.
The world’s largest single serving of fries weighed over 1.5 tons.
In some countries fries are served with mayonnaise, in others with ketchup or chili sauce.

items.title: Potassium source
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports heart and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: When cooked properly (not over‑fried) potatoes retain vitamin C, important for immunity.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: The skin of the potato provides dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Fries supply fast‑acting carbohydrates, useful for intense physical activity.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Potatoes contain carotenoids and polyphenols with antioxidant properties.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Deep‑frying makes fries calorie‑dense and high in unhealthy fats, which can contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Cooking at high temperatures can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Excessive salting raises the risk of hypertension.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fries are served hot, typically in paper containers or boxes. They can be dipped in ketchup, mayonnaise, tartar sauce, cheese sauce, or seasoned with herbs and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked fries are best eaten immediately. If needed, store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days; reheat in an oven to restore crispness.
